key_insight: Large language models can help automate reproducibility checks in the social and behavioral sciences by comparing their analyses to the original studies' claims. This suggests reproducibility assessment may become faster, cheaper, and more scalable.
problem_solved: Traditional reproducibility reviews require independent researchers to reanalyze data manually, which is time-consuming, costly, and hard to scale across many studies.
method: Collected 76 published studies with predefined claims from the social and behavioral sciences.
Used large language models to generate or assist with analysis for each study.
Compared the LLM-based results against the original published findings to assess whether the claims could be recovered.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows LLMs can support research auditing and meta-science workflows beyond text generation. It highlights a practical use case where models reduce expert workload and enable larger-scale evaluation of scientific reliability.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: original study vs. LLM-assisted reproducibility check
Workflow chart showing data input, LLM analysis, and claim comparison
Bar chart or heatmap summarizing agreement between LLM results and original findings
Icon set for speed, scale, and research verification
paper_title: Automated reproducibility assessments in the social and behavioral sciences using large language models
paper_authors: Tobias Holtdirk, Pietro Marcolongo, Anna Steinberg Schulten, Felix Henninger, Stefan Rose
